International Harvester Corporation (IH). IH takes particular exception to the EPA analysis that the proposed standards for exhaust emissions can be achieved without fuel economy penalty. IH believes that there is significant information available showing that the reduction of NOx to the low levels proposed by EPA are not possible by MY 1979 without an appreciable loss in fuel economy. IH estimated that the 26 percent reduction in NOx from the 1977 level to the new level proposed by EPA for 1979 (3.1 to 2.3 grams per mile) will result in a 10-15 percent fuel economy penalty.
•
General Motors Corporation (GM). GM stated that a loss of 0.9 mpg or 5.1 percent is estimated to occur when vehicles are recalibrated to meet the more stringent MY 1979 light duty truck emission standards of 1.7/18/2.3.
GM concluded that their emissions penalty estimate is considered to be very representative of anticipated losses since the vehicle configurations they tested and their emission control hardware are similar to that which will be manufactured in MY 1979.
